Usage: drive page [flags]

Serve the live batches as a web page their owner opens: each session's goal, where it stands, its pull requests, and what waits on them.

Each request reads every live batch, each driver's current one, on one
page: the questions waiting on the owner first, then each batch's sessions,
closed ones included. --batch or --driver shows one batch instead. It
changes nothing. A card's anchor is the batch's name and the session's
label, such as #2026-10-27/T1, so a link opens one session's card. A read
is reused for 30 seconds; one that takes longer than 20 seconds is answered
from the batch's record while it finishes.

It runs until stopped, and exits once the drive binary it runs is
replaced, so a supervisor such as launchd restarts it on the new one. It
answers anyone who reaches the address: on the mini, a loopback address
that tailscale serve publishes on the tailnet.

Flags:
      --listen=ADDR    The address to serve it on (default: 127.0.0.1:8792).

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help           Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME     Act in this batch, as drive prints its name, instead of the driver's current
                       one. It may stand anywhere on the line.
      --driver=NAME    Act as this driver, in its current batch: a chat driver is named by its
                       webhook. Where drivers each drive a batch, every command names one. It may
                       stand anywhere on the line.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner
